profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.profile: This is the rare file where the tee ball is the suspicious part and the irons are the adult in the room. The long game has been noisy, but the approach play is doing obscene work and dragging the whole bag out of the ditch. When the putter cooperates, the whole thing looks scary fast; when it doesn’t, it still somehow hangs around because the wedges keep cleaning up the mess. Two starts is a tiny sample, sure, but the golf already has a clear shape: hit it crooked, then flick on God mode with the irons and act like that’s normal.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.tagline: TEE BOX MENACE WITH A SHORT GAME SURPRISE
profiles.profile: This dude keeps showing up like a guy who can win ugly, pretty, or by accident, which is infuriating for everyone else. The driver and irons are both loud enough to kick in the door, and the putter has been doing its part without making a scene. The weird part is that the big picture keeps surviving the occasional messy patch, because the scoring never really falls apart when the driver gets a little reckless. Five starts in and the profile is simple: if you let him spray it and still reach the greens, he’ll bury you with enough birdies to make your scorecard look like it got mugged.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: This bag is basically a demolition project with excellent upholstery. The driver keeps showing up like it owns the place, and the short game has been bailing out enough chaos to keep the card from going full dumpster fire. The irons are more of a mood than a plan, which is why the whole operation can look terrifyingly good one day and a little swampy the next. Over the window, the recurring story is simple: if the tee ball is loud and the wedges are sharp, he can bully a leaderboard; if not, the putter has to start doing unpaid overtime.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.profile: This profile is all about survival golf with a surprisingly nasty little short-game engine. The tee ball and irons are decent enough to keep the round on the rails, but the real damage comes from scrambling and putting when the hole starts trying to mug him. He’s not exactly bullying the field off the tee; he’s more like the guy who keeps stealing par after par while everyone else is busy inventing self-harm. The shape is pretty clear: when the wedges get hot, the whole bag suddenly looks better than it has any right to.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This is the most backwards golf in the batch, in the best and dumbest way. The iron play keeps trying to drag the score back to civilization while the tee ball and putter take turns setting fire to the room. It’s not clean, and it’s definitely not calm, but the results keep hanging around because the middle of the bag can still make the thing work when everything else gets weird. The whole identity here is volatility: there’s enough good ball-striking to survive, enough chaos to annoy you, and just enough putts falling to keep the wreck from becoming a full funeral.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.profile: This one lives in the funhouse where one part of the bag is trying to save golf and the other part is apparently trying to get it arrested. The short game can get spicy enough to rescue a round, but the tee ball has been a recurring tax, and the numbers spend a lot of time looking like they’re arguing in the parking lot. When the putter gets warm, he can absolutely steal a card; when it doesn’t, the missed tee shots turn the whole thing into a trench fight. Four starts in and the identity is already clear: messy off the tee, dangerous enough around the greens to stay annoying.
